seasonalNotes: Cherry blossom late Mar–Apr. Rainy season (tsuyu) Jun–Jul. Hot humid summers. Typhoon season Aug–Oct. Beautiful autumn foliage Oct–Nov. Cold dry winters.

personas.name: Tokyo Office Day
personas.tagline: Metro, bento, and izakaya after work
personas.description: Commutes from Shibuya to Marunouchi by metro. Bento lunch from the depachika, afternoon meetings, and izakaya with colleagues after work.

stops.title: Folding umbrella — check weather
stops.description: Tokyo rain is unpredictable. Always carry one.
stops.action: Check the weather app and pack a folding umbrella.
stops.context: Rain can start suddenly in Tokyo, especially in spring and summer.
stops.wellbeing: Wear waterproof shoes if rain is likely.
stops.motivation: Being prepared ensures a comfortable commute.
stops.localization: Umbrellas are sold at every convenience store.
stops.transition: Walk to Shibuya Station for your commute.
stops.feedback: Did this tip help you stay dry today?

stops.title: Top up Suica at station
stops.description: Balance was ¥340. Top up ¥2000 at the machine.
stops.action: Check your Suica balance and top up at the ticket machine.
stops.context: Morning rush means long lines at the machines.
stops.wellbeing: Keep your wallet and phone secure in the crowd.
stops.motivation: A topped-up card means a smooth commute!
stops.feedback: Did this reminder help you avoid delays?

stops.title: Morning meeting — 5F conference room
stops.description: Q3 review. Bring USB backup of slides.
stops.action: Arrive 5 minutes early and check the projector setup.
stops.context: Meetings in Japan start on time—punctuality is key.
stops.wellbeing: Have a bottle of water ready for the meeting.
stops.motivation: Preparedness leads to a successful meeting!
stops.localization: Reception can help with directions if needed.
stops.transition: After the meeting, head to Daimaru for lunch.
stops.feedback: Did this meeting tip help you feel ready?

stops.title: Bento from depachika
stops.description: Daimaru basement. Get the salmon bento before it sells out.
stops.action: Arrive before noon for the best selection. Try a seasonal bento.
stops.context: Depachika food halls are busiest at lunchtime.
stops.wellbeing: Choose a balanced meal for sustained energy.
stops.motivation: A good lunch keeps you productive all afternoon!
stops.localization: Staff can help with recommendations in simple English.
stops.transition: Return to the office for afternoon work.
stops.feedback: Did this lunch tip help you enjoy Japanese food?

stops.title: Submit monthly report before leaving
stops.description: Deadline 6 PM. Send before heading out.
stops.action: Finish your report and double-check for errors before sending.
stops.context: Many offices close promptly at 6 PM.
stops.wellbeing: Take a short break before your evening plans.
stops.motivation: Completing tasks on time means a stress-free evening!
stops.localization: Printers and scanners available on each floor.
stops.transition: Head to Yurakucho for dinner with colleagues.
stops.feedback: Did this reminder help you finish your work on time?

stops.title: Izakaya with the team
stops.description: Torikizoku near Yurakucho. First round on bucho.
stops.action: Order a drink and toast with your team. Try yakitori if you haven’t before.
stops.context: Izakayas are lively—expect a fun, social atmosphere.
stops.wellbeing: Drink water between rounds and eat before drinking.
stops.motivation: Celebrate your hard work with your team!
stops.localization: Menus often have pictures and some English.
stops.transition: Plan your route home or to your next stop.
stops.feedback: Did this dinner tip help you enjoy your evening?

personas.name: Kyoto Temple Trail
personas.description: A full day in Kyoto: Fushimi Inari at dawn, Arashiyama bamboo grove, golden pavilion, matcha in Gion, and lantern-lit Higashiyama.

stops.title: Fushimi Inari — go at sunrise
stops.description: No crowds before 7 AM. Thousands of vermilion torii.
stops.action: Arrive before sunrise for quiet photos. Bring a flashlight for the early walk.
stops.context: The shrine is open 24/7, but shops open later.
stops.wellbeing: Stay hydrated and wear comfortable shoes.
stops.motivation: Start your day with peace and tradition!
stops.localization: English signage available. Toilets at the entrance.
stops.transition: Take the JR line to Arashiyama for the bamboo grove.
stops.feedback: Did this shrine tip help you enjoy Kyoto?

stops.title: Bamboo grove — morning light
stops.description: Arashiyama. Visit by 9 AM for empty photos.
stops.action: Arrive early for fewer crowds. Bring a camera for the best shots.
stops.context: The grove is busiest after 10 AM.
stops.wellbeing: Watch your step on uneven paths.
stops.transition: Take a bus or taxi to Kinkaku-ji.
stops.feedback: Did this walk help you enjoy Kyoto’s nature?

stops.title: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
stops.description: Stunning reflection on the lake. ¥400 entry.
stops.action: Buy your ticket at the gate. Take photos from the designated spots.
stops.context: The pavilion is busiest midday—arrive early for fewer crowds.
stops.wellbeing: Use sunscreen and wear a hat in summer.
stops.transition: Head to Gion for matcha and sweets.
stops.feedback: Did this temple tip help you enjoy your visit?

stops.title: Matcha + wagashi in Gion
stops.description: Tsujiri matcha house. Try the matcha parfait.
stops.action: Order a matcha parfait and try seasonal wagashi.
stops.context: Gion is famous for traditional tea houses.
stops.transition: Walk to Kiyomizu-dera for sunset views.
stops.feedback: Did this tea tip help you enjoy Gion?

stops.title: Kiyomizu-dera before sunset
stops.description: Wooden terrace with panoramic city views.
stops.action: Arrive before sunset for the best views. Bring a camera.
stops.context: The terrace can get crowded—be patient for photos.
stops.motivation: End your day with a stunning view!
stops.localization: Audio guides available. Toilets at the entrance.
stops.feedback: Did this temple tip help you enjoy Kyoto?

stops.title: Evening stroll — Higashiyama streets
stops.action: Shop for souvenirs and enjoy the lantern-lit streets.
stops.context: Shops close by 7 PM—plan your purchases early.
stops.localization: English spoken at most souvenir shops.
stops.transition: Return to your hotel or next destination.
stops.feedback: Did this stroll help you enjoy Kyoto’s history?
